ops.statement: A delegated Commander dispatched by an Admiral runs as a HARNESS TEAMMATE, and a teammate can spawn neither NAMED subagents ('Teammates cannot spawn other teammates - the team roster is flat') nor BACKGROUND subagents ('In-process teammates cannot spawn background agents'). Both restrictions contradict standing doctrine: commander-core's mission-frame section requires every dispatched background subagent to be told to deliver via SendMessage (impossible - an unnamed subagent has no address and cannot message a teammate parent), and the delegated skill instructs polling a crew's result artifact in a loop while waiting (impossible - the synchronous call blocks). Neither is a blocker: multiple synchronous Agent calls in ONE message do run concurrently, and the result-artifact file is a fine delivery channel. But each restriction costs a failed-dispatch discovery round-trip.

ops.bank_reason: One delegated run, one harness configuration. Needs a second delegated Commander in a different epic to hit the same two refusals before the doctrine text is edited -- it is possible the restriction is specific to how this Admiral dispatched its wave rather than to delegated Commanders generally.

ops.statement: The `! <command>` bash-negation postcondition pattern (prove a guard CORRECTLY fails) inverts silently when the negation is applied to a PROBE rather than to the guard itself. `! A || B` parses as `(! A) || B`: when probe A fails because the artifact does not exist yet, `! A` is true, `||` short-circuits, and the whole list exits 0, which the engine records as PASS. The check whose entire purpose is 'the guard fires on bad input' is then satisfied by never writing the guard. Rule: the negation must wrap the invocation that must fail, and nothing else. A plain positive command naming a test that asserts the failure internally is usually safer -- a missing file or missing test id exits 4, which correctly FAILS.
ops.grounding: .agent-work/300/PLAN_CRITIC_DISPOSITION.md finding B1, reproduced by the Commander running the string verbatim in the worktree with no lint and no test present: exit 0. Compare lesson:prove-command-fails-postcondition, which introduced the `!` wrapper and is correct -- this is its adjacent failure mode, not a disconfirmation of it.
ops.bank_reason: Graduation basis is stronger than a single instance, and stronger than repeated successes would be: this ONE wave produced both halves of the technique's evidence. #303 confirmed lesson:prove-command-fails-postcondition from a SUCCESS case (three postconditions using the wrapper, all satisfied on first advance, no rework) while #300 produced this FAILURE case (the wrapper bound to a probe, exit 0 with nothing built, engine records PASS). A success and a failure for one technique in one wave is a better basis than two successes, because only the failure teaches WHAT IS BEING NEGATED, which is the entire subtlety. Bank rather than graduate immediately only because #311 is already open to document the wrapper inline in the plan template and is the right home -- this lesson should graduate INTO that documentation (with the negative example, per the comment posted there), not into a separate doctrine line. Retire it when #311 lands.

ops.statement: A design-it-twice panel varies what it is TOLD to vary and inherits everything it is not, so a wrong assumption SHARED by every candidate is the one thing the method structurally cannot surface -- and unanimity on it reads as strong evidence when it is only common inheritance. Two distinct sources of false convergence: (a) the BRIEF'S OWN fixed constraints handed back as if independently derived, and (b) PRIOR ART borrowed for one aspect (a record's grammar) and silently carried along for another (where records live). Two cheap mitigations, both to be run at convergence, before the recommendation is floated: run `git check-ignore` (or the equivalent environment check) on every path any candidate names; and explicitly ask what EVERY candidate assumed in common, then verify THAT rather than only what they disagreed on. Re-grade each convergence as derived or inherited and report only the derived ones as panel evidence.
ops.grounding: Two independent panels in epic-298 wave 0. #301: all four candidates chose `.agent-work/episodes/` for the store, which is gitignored at .gitignore:1 with zero tracked files -- violating the settled markdown-in-git ruling and destroying the store at worktree sweep; caught only at a deliverable-path check after the comparison was 'complete'. #300 (.agent-work/300/DIT-COMPARISON.md, ADDENDUM): running the audit on its own 3-author panel retracted one of five reported convergences ('metadata only' was the Commander's own brief constraint echoed back, not independent agreement), found an unquestioned inherited declaration LOCATION whose per-work-area instantiation creates a legitimate committed-vs-instantiated disagreement a naive drift check would misreport, and found that all three authors had verified the blob-OID identity only under the current `* text=auto` .gitattributes with no -text/binary exemption -- a silent-divergence hazard closed via the engine's amend verb as postcondition g1-implement.c7, verified in both directions.
ops.bank_reason: Two occurrences in one wave, but both in the same epic under the same Admiral and the same brief-authoring habits, so the shared cause may be this epic's brief style rather than the method. RATIFIED DISPOSITION (Admiral, epic-298): do NOT wait to act. The two mitigations run on every panel NOW, as a convergence step -- doing beats documenting while the sample is two. What waits is only the WRITE-UP into design-it-twice-brief.md, which needs a third instance from a DIFFERENT epic so it graduates on evidence rather than on how memorable these two were. This resolves the usual bank-or-graduate tension as a false binary: the practice and its documentation graduate on different evidence thresholds.
